_about: How FL Studio thinks - core ideas in plain words (our own notes).

cards.title: Patterns, the playlist and pattern/song mode
cards.summary: A pattern holds notes for any channels; the playlist arranges patterns, audio clips and automation clips into a song. Pattern mode loops the selected pattern; song mode plays the playlist (toggle with L).
cards.beginner: Think of patterns as building blocks (a drum loop, a bassline) and the playlist as the timeline where you stack those blocks into a song. If pressing play only loops one bar, you're in pattern mode - press L.
tips: One pattern per instrument part keeps arranging flexible.
Patterns can be split by channel (PATTERNS menu) when one holds several instruments.

cards.title: Channels vs mixer tracks
cards.summary: Channels (channel rack) make sound: samples and instruments. Mixer tracks process sound: effects, levels, routing. Each channel plays through the mixer track number in its Track box.
cards.beginner: Instruments live in the channel rack; effects live in the mixer. Give each instrument its own mixer track so you can EQ and balance it on its own.

cards.title: Mixer routing: sends, buses, sidechain
cards.summary: Select a mixer track, and the arrows at the bottom of the other tracks show where it sends. Left-click an arrow to add a send; right-click for 'Route to this track only' (bus) or 'Sidechain to this track'.
tips: Send amount: the small knob that appears on the destination's arrow.
Master is track 0; a track not sent anywhere is silent.

cards.title: Automation clips
cards.summary: A playlist clip that moves one control over time. It shows as a channel in the channel rack and a clip in the playlist; point curves can be smooth, stepped, pulses and more.
tips: Right-click points for curve types; Alt/Ctrl change how drags behave.
An automation clip's own settings include an LFO to generate repeating curves.

cards.title: Piano roll note properties
cards.summary: Every note has velocity, release, pan, mod X/Y, fine pitch and length, edited in the event lane under the piano roll. Notes can be slide (glide to the next pitch) or porta.
tips: Double-click a note to edit its properties numerically.
Slide notes glide the channel's pitch; porta needs portamento on the channel/synth.

cards.title: Snap (grid) and quantize
cards.summary: The magnet menu in each window sets the grid notes/clips snap to (bar, beat, step, cell, none). Hold Alt while dragging to bypass it. Quantize moves existing notes onto the grid.

cards.title: FL editions and what they include
cards.summary: Fruity < Producer < Signature < All Plugins. Producer adds full audio recording/clips, Edison, Slicex, Sytrus, Maximus; Signature adds Gross Beat, Pitcher, NewTone, NewTime, Harmless; All Plugins adds Harmor, Sakura and the other synths. Unowned plugins run as demos.
tips: fl-headless never assumes an edition: set it with flh_setup; flh_catalog decides ownership per plugin.
Upgrades are lifetime-free within an edition (Image-Line's lifetime free updates).

cards.title: Loudness (LUFS) and true peak
aliases: how loud should my song be
cards.summary: LUFS measures perceived loudness over the song. Streaming services turn louder songs down, so about -14 LUFS integrated with true peak under -1 dBTP is a safe target; louder masters lose punch and gain nothing there.
cards.beginner: LUFS is a loudness number for the whole song. Around -14 LUFS is what most streaming sites play at; going louder just gets turned down and sounds squashed.
cards.pro: Integrated LUFS over the song, short-term for sections; -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP is a neutral streaming target (club and some genres master hotter). Measure after the limiter; fl-headless finals measure and report both.
tips: Genres differ: club/EDM masters often sit louder, classical/ambient quieter - follow the collection profile.

cards.title: Gain staging and headroom
cards.summary: Keep tracks well below 0 dB (peaks around -6 to -10 dB) and the master peaking under 0 before the limiter. FL's mixer is floating-point, so internal overs don't clip until the output, but plugins react to level.
tips: Lower channel volumes (or Fruity Balance) instead of pushing the master down.
Red master peaks in the final file = audible clipping.

cards.title: Latency and plugin delay compensation
cards.summary: Some plugins (look-ahead limiters, linear-phase EQs) add delay. FL compensates automatically when the plugin reports it; for recording, use a small buffer and avoid heavy plugins on armed tracks.

cards.title: Playlist tracks are not mixer tracks
cards.summary: Playlist tracks are just lanes to place clips on - any clip can go on any lane. Sound goes through mixer tracks (set by the channel), not by which playlist lane a clip sits in.
cards.beginner: Moving a clip to another playlist row doesn't change its sound or effects; the mixer track does.

cards.title: Swing and groove
cards.summary: The channel rack's swing knob delays every other step for a shuffle feel; per-channel shift and the piano roll's quantize/randomize tools add groove and looseness.
tips: Swing affects step-sequenced notes; piano-roll notes need quantize with swing or manual nudges.

cards.title: Multi-output plugins (drums to separate tracks)
cards.summary: Plugins with several outputs (FPC, drum samplers) can send each pad/part to its own mixer track: enable outputs in the plugin wrapper's processing settings, then pick mixer tracks.

cards.title: The plugin wrapper (settings around every plugin)
cards.summary: Every plugin window has a toolbar (presets, menu) and a settings page (the cog): MIDI ports, outputs, processing options, and 'Browse parameters' to find automatable controls.
tips: Browse parameters lists all automatable controls of a VST - right-click one there to create an automation clip.

cards.title: Timebase (PPQ)
cards.summary: PPQ is how many ticks a quarter note has (FL default 96; higher = finer timing). Set it in project settings early; fl-headless reads it from the .flp.

cards.title: Performance mode (live clip launching)
cards.summary: Playlist performance mode turns playlist tracks into live clip launchers you trigger from a controller or the mouse; recording captures the performance.

cards.title: FL Cloud (sounds, mastering, plugin subscription)
cards.summary: Image-Line's online service built into recent FL versions: a sound/loop library, online mastering, distribution, and a plugin subscription tier.

cards.title: Picker panel (playlist)
cards.summary: The panel at the playlist's left lists every pattern, audio clip and automation clip; click one to make it the clip you paint, drag it into the playlist.
